## What you need

- **Must (headline):** Python (production), LLM APIs & tool calling, Agents & tool use, Prompt & context design.
- **Important (headline):** Agent reliability (durable state, budgets, approvals), MCP (Model Context Protocol), Containment (DLP, sandboxing, egress), LLM evaluation (golden sets, calibrated judges, CI gates), LLM security (prompt injection, OWASP), Agent frameworks (LangGraph, Agents SDKs), Human-in-the-loop design.
- **Full inventory:** 73 skills (Must 5 · Important 18 · Should 31 · Optional 17 · Avoid 2), each with its evidence and posting keywords: [agentic-ai-engineer.md](../../03-skills-and-tech/inventories/agentic-ai-engineer.md).
- **Prerequisites:** Usually an AI Engineer title in practice; the standalone title is small (~66 + 28 postings in 90 days)
- **Credentials (tie-breakers, not skills):** AWS Certified Generative AI Developer – Professional (AIP-C01) (Optional: tie-breaker in services channels). Whether one is worth it: [credential ROI](../../04-certifications/credential-roi.md).
- What to learn first and what to drop across roles: [skills radar](../../03-skills-and-tech/skills-radar.md); in what order: [learning roadmaps](../../03-skills-and-tech/learning-roadmaps.md).

## How to prove it

- **What the evidence asks for:** An agent with human approval, sandboxed tools, deterministic trace replay and failure-injection tests (timeouts, malformed arguments, prompt injection), reporting cost per task
- **Project archetypes that cover the most of its Must and Important skills** (Grade M): [P2 Reliable agent: approvals, sandboxed tools, replay, failure injection](../../05-portfolio/project-archetypes.md#p2) (81%); [P1 Evaluated RAG system over a real corpus](../../05-portfolio/project-archetypes.md#p1) (42%); [P10 Red-team suite in CI against a working agent](../../05-portfolio/project-archetypes.md#p10) (35%). One project rarely covers a role; [job-search strategy §2.6](../../06-job-search/job-search-strategy.md#26-the-constraints-that-bind-first) computes the smallest sets that do.
- How verifiable the proof must be, and what to publish: [proof-of-work standards](../../05-portfolio/proof-of-work-standards.md).

## How you are interviewed

- **Track: Application.** It tests RAG with access control, agent loop control, evaluation architecture, context management. Source: career/02-roles/role-catalog.md §8.2 (T1-03, T0-14).
- **Practise:** the [application prep pack](../../08-interviewing/prep-packs.md#application-pack), plus the behavioural and coding packs.
- Classify the loop first, then prepare by round: [interview loops](../../08-interviewing/interview-loops.md).

## Résumé

- **Variant:** A1 (Applied GenAI Engineering). Headline pattern: "AI Engineer | LLM systems, RAG, agents, evals".
- **Keywords to mirror, only when true:** agentic AI, agents, multi-agent, LangGraph (35.8% of Agentic AI Engineer postings), LangChain, MCP, tool calling
- **Leave out or reframe:** AutoGen (dormant); CrewAI as a headline (absent from tier-1 lab postings); demo agents with no failure handling
- The concise skills section for this role: [résumé skills matrix](../../06-job-search/resume-skills-matrix.md#resume-agentic-ai-engineer).
